sophia: Quick heads-up — opened a docs PR to clarify autoscale cooldown behavior for Reserved capacity pools: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4021
kevin: +1. Can you paste the SDK snippet you want included in the 'Reserved capacity' section so I can slot it in?

sophia: sure — planning to add a minimal SDK example showing per-tenant cooldown override (note: runtime behavior caveat below):
```python
# SDK example: set tenant autoscale overrides
client.dedicated.capacity.update(
  tenant_id='acme-123',
  autoscale={ 'cooldown_seconds': 300, 'min_replicas': 2, 'max_replicas': 10 }
)
```

taylor: LGTM as an example, but important: runtime currently enforces cooldown at the pool level. We need a sentence explaining the fallback rule (tenant override may be ignored if pool cooldown window is active). pinging @elaine for confirmation.
elaine: confirmed — runtime semantics: cooldown is enforced at pool granularity. If a tenant requests a faster scale-down than the pool allows, the pool-level cooldown wins. We should add one short bullet and a tiny migration note.
kevin: can we call out SLA implications too? like: "tenant cooldowns do not change SLA guarantees; they are hints subject to pool policy." I'll draft wording.
sophia: thanks — I'll add a short migration note: existing tenant overrides will remain visible in the UI and API but may be ignored until pool-level policy is relaxed. Also adding an ascii diagram to make the hierarchy clear.
sam: staging preview for the PR is up: https://deploy-preview-4021--docs.redwood.ai — look at the 'Reserved capacity' section under "Autoscaling".
docs-bot: link-checker completed — 1 warning (internal anchor changed).
pr-bot: PR 4021 updated: reviewers requested: @kevin @taylor @elaine. CI passed.
sophia: assigning @kevin to refine copy, @taylor to verify the example and edge-case phrasing. Can we aim to merge by EOD tomorrow? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kevin: I can do copy by EOD. I'll add a one-line changelog note under "Docs updates".
taylor: I'll run the example against the staging runtime tomorrow morning and report back with an explicit note if behavior differs.
sophia: perfect — thanks all. Small ask: if you spot any ambiguous words, use the inline suggestion flow on the PR rather than long threads. :sparkles:
